case_title: Anil @ Bawa v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the accused alleged the victim had an evil eye on the women of the accused's family (motive alleged in FIR); the defence alleged the victim tried to outrage a woman's modesty
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.148 r/w s.302
evidence_type: Eyewitness (father of victim), medical evidence, investigation witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Armed group; large number of injuries (ten sharp-edged injuries plus lathi blows); death on the spot
trial_court_outcome: Convicted all six accused; for appellants: life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 each (default 3 months SI) under s.302 r/w s.149; RI one year under s.148 r/w s.302
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction affirmed for remaining five accused (one accused acquitted by High Court for benefit of doubt)
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.149); IPC s.148 r/w s.302
neutral_facts: The victim's father reported that the victim had gone to a village gathering place and, when he did not return, went with two others to search for him. Near a veterinary hospital they saw the victim confronted by several men, some armed with lathis and others with swords. The men said the victim should be taught a lesson for having an evil eye on the women of the accused's family. The attackers struck the victim with sword blows to the head, hand and face and with lathi blows, and inflicted injuries on the hands, stomach, waist and chest, then fled. The victim died at the scene. The First Information Report was lodged early the next morning, about seven hours after the incident. A doctor's medical examination recorded ten sharp-edged injuries and lathi contusions and bruises on the back, right side, front chest and both arms. The victim's father was an eyewitness to the beating. He stated that he became unwell for about two hours after the victim's death, which explained the delay in lodging the report. The defence contended that the victim had tried to molest a woman and was beaten by villagers. Two named witnesses were not examined. Eleven prosecution witnesses were examined, including investigating and medical witnesses.
physical_harm: Death on the spot; ten sharp-edged injuries and multiple lathi contusions and bruises
number_of_offences: 2 charged (as reflected in convictions; separate charge framing not stated); 2 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court; court noted the accused came armed
motive: alleged: victim had an evil eye on the women of the accused's family
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of the victim's father (PW5), corroborated by medical evidence of Dr. Naresh Dahiya (PW7)
witness_credibility: Father-eyewitness (PW5) found reliable and truthful; no enmity; delay in FIR satisfactorily explained; no inherent improbabilities
post_offence_conduct: Fled from the scene after the beating (as narrated in FIR; court did not separately comment)
trial_duration: offence: 4.7.2003; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 06.08.2009; Supreme Court: 25.02.2016
legal_representation: Accused: Pushpinder Singh, Kumar Kumkay, Aruneshwar Gupta, Amarjit Singh Bedi (Advs.). State of Haryana: S.U.K. Sagar, Vishwa Pal Singh, Naresh Bakshi, Rao Ranjit (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR registered 5.7.2003; investigation completed; 11 prosecution witnesses examined; 8 defence witnesses examined
procedural_irregularity: Two named witnesses not examined; court held adverse inference depends on facts and was not warranted; no unfair trial found
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted six accused. High Court: affirmed convictions of five, acquitted one. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Ocular evidence of PW5 is supported by medical evidence; conviction proper; non-examined witnesses were won over by the accused; defence evidence considered
defence_argument: False implication; victim tried to outrage a woman's modesty and was beaten by villagers; belated FIR; adverse inference for non-examination of two named witnesses; version of a related and chance witness not acceptable (Bahal Singh)
legal_principle_applied: Reliable ocular evidence corroborated by medical evidence sustains conviction; adverse inference for non-examination depends on facts; fair trial assessed on facts of each case
precedent_relied_upon: State of U.P. v. Jaggo alias Jagdish, AIR 1971 SC 1586; Bahal Singh v. State of Haryana, AIR 1976 SC 2032
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused took law into their own hands; beat the victim mercilessly and intentionally; multiple weapon injuries
